items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: I’ve not heard that definition before... When I first came across this word in a really great book called Free Play by Stephen Nachmanovich who is a sort of free improvising violinist... he’s written a wonderful book about creativity

ctx.x: And I went wooh. It makes me think of music, especially the genre of music you play. Because sometimes there’s not answers to these questions we’re talking about.

Absolutely. Yeah. I’ve not heard that definition before, and I can’t remember the exact wording for the definition. When I first came across this word in a really great book called Free Play by Stephen Nachmanovich who is a sort of free improvising violinist, although I think he’s classically trained, but he’s written a wonderful book about creativity and spontaneity and what that means in our world. And in that he uses this term © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

“satori” which I think his definition is something like a moment of presence away from the clutter of the egoic mind, the thinking, analytic, rationalizing mind. And for me when I first put my trio together it was very much a choice to move away from the music I’d been playing prior to that which was very sort of changes-based I suppose, more in the American Songbook tradition, and I wanted to do something totally different I think, much more spacious, freeing, sort of let go of all of the structures that you get…
